finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of owner because the authorized() result is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete another user's project.
finding.source: req.params.id (api.js:17) selects an arbitrary project; caller is any authenticated user with req.user set upstream.

trace.note: authorized() returns a boolean predicate: ownerId === user.id || isAdmin === true
project loaded by id from URL with no ownership scoping
authorized(req.user, project) called but return value ignored; no throw, no return, no if-guard
responds 204, so the attacker gets no error signal

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is correct as a predicate but not enforced at the call site. No ownership check in the route. The PUT route at api.js:25 uses authorize(), which throws (api.js:4-10), so it is enforced there. No auth middleware is defined in this repo; upstream req.user population was not verifiable.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. The only ownership check, authorized() at api.js:12-14, returns a boolean, and the call at api.js:18 discards it. The throwing variant authorize() (api.js:4-10) is not called in the DELETE route; it is used only by the PUT route at api.js:25. No ownership scoping on the lookup at api.js:17. No auth middleware exists in this repo, so upstream req.user population could not be checked, but any upstream middleware would only establish authentication, not ownership.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:18 calls authorized(req.user, project) as a bare statement, so its false result has no effect, and api.js:19 deletes the project for any caller whose req.user is set (api.js:13 returns false for non-owners and non-admins, but nothing acts on it). The attacker is an authenticated low-privilege user, which is the claimed threat model, and the deletion power is not one they already hold.
